answer: Sybil attacks fail here because attestation weight only accrues to identities peers verified through sustained work. A new identity starts at zero and climbs a slow ladder: peer review, bonds, history. Like drilling through a glacier, each verified layer costs time and real payment, so mass-producing identities never scales. Peers check claims against a shared atlas of attested records. A walnut deposit earns nothing until peers confirm interaction. A farm must fund N reviewed histories, and its clones fail checks by citing each other in tight loops. Cost per vote outgrows identity count.
